title: Impact of an Established Physiotherapy Protocol on Outcomes Following Treatment of Mandibular Condylar Process Fractures
summary:
Fractures of the lower jaw near the jaw joint can cause pain and make it difficult to open the mouth and chew. After surgery, guided movement exercises and other supportive treatments aim to restore mobility. However, it remains unclear how much a structured treatment programme improves recovery.
The study investigates whether a twelve-week treatment programme after surgery improves jaw movement, reduces pain, and makes everyday activities easier. It also assesses how treatment affects quality of life and how participants experience their care.

Methods

The study at the University Medical Centre Mainz includes people over 18 years of age who have undergone surgery for a fracture of the lower jaw near the jaw joint on one or both sides. Participation is voluntary and requires written consent.

The treatment programme is provided in cooperation with a local practice in Mainz and consists of 18 sessions lasting 30 minutes each over twelve weeks. It includes guided movement exercises, exercises to perform at home, and treatments to reduce pain and swelling.
Before treatment and at a follow-up assessment three months after surgery, participants are assessed to determine how well they can open their mouths and move their jaws, and what symptoms they experience. They also complete questionnaires about their quality of life, oral health, and experiences of care. Their results are compared with those of people who do not receive a corresponding treatment programme after surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged over 18 years with mandibular condylar process fractures (all classifications, unilateral or bilateral).
Exclusion criteria:
Pathological fractures
Previous surgery or a history of mandibular condylar process fracture
Chronic pain or known temporomandibular disorders
Pre-existing neurological conditions (e.g., fibromyalgia, multiple sclerosis)
Pre-existing psychiatric disorders
Intellectual or physical impairments that limit adherence to the study protocol
